Dear Dr. McLaren,
Re: 
 Mr. 
Michael  Weir
, DOB: 20/09/1970
       Thank you for seeing 
Mr.Weir
, a 44-year-old real 
state
 agent, whose symptoms and signs are suggestive of multiple 
sclerosis
. Your expert management including ordering an MRI would be appreciated.
Mr. Weir, who is married with 3 children, is smoker and overweight. Regarding his past medical history, he suffers from depression for which he has been maintained on Zoloft since September 2012.
On 29/06/2014, Mr. Weir presented with fatigue and stress. His examination was free apart from mild hypotension and high BMI. The appropriate investigations including CBC and lipid profile were requested.
One week later, 
Mr.Weil
 reported having progressive fatigue and 
a 
newly developed weakness in his left leg. His investigations 
showed leucopenia
 and anemia along with hypercholesterolemia for 
which a
 three -month follow up was recommended. Please note
,
 he was compliant with his a
ntidepressant. Therefore, he was advised to comply 
with
 a healthier life-style and consulted about stopping smoking.
On review today, Mr. Weil attended my clinic complaining of dizziness and history of 
two attacks of syncope
 coincided with 
a 
continuing stress. Additionally, he reported having tingling sensation in his hands along with persistent left leg weakness. Despite of being compliant to a better-life style, he has suffered from fatigue and occasional constipation. Unfortunately, he still smokes. Upon examination, 
loss of sharp and blunt sensation in his both hands with diminished left patellar reflex was
 detected. Hence a CT brain was ordered.
Should be there any queries, please contact me 
Yours sincerely,
Doctor
